patch.objective: Assess a client's capacity for decisions about money, treatment and consent, including emancipation and age of consent
secondaryObjectives: Explain confidentiality and privileged communication, their limits, and how HIPAA protects health information

sources.cite: RCW 71.34.530, Outpatient treatment of adolescent (2019 c 381 s 6): 'Any adolescent may request and receive outpatient treatment without the consent of the adolescent's parent'; parental authorization is required for outpatient treatment of a minor under thirteen
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on the Legislature's page for the section (summarizing fetch with the short quote). The section does not address notifying parents.

sources.cite: RCW 70.02.240 (2024 c 209 s 33): when a minor's mental health information may be disclosed without consent, including to a parent in listed circumstances, to law enforcement in a crisis posing a significant and imminent risk to the public, and to a person whose health and safety has been threatened
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on the Legislature's page (summarizing fetch). The summary did not settle when a parent may see records of outpatient treatment a 13-to-17-year-old consented to herself; the case therefore promises her no more than it can (honest limits, no call to her parents without talking with her first, except in an emergency).

sources.cite: Appelbaum PS. Assessment of patients' competence to consent to treatment. N Engl J Med 2007;357(18):1834-1840, as summarized by the AMA Journal of Ethics (August 2008): four abilities: expressing a choice, understanding the relevant information, appreciating the consequences for oneself, and reasoning about the options
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the AMA Journal of Ethics summary (summarizing fetch); the NEJM article itself was not opened.

sources.cite: NASW Code of Ethics (2021 revision): 1.02 self-determination, limited when clients' actions 'pose a serious, foreseeable, and imminent risk to themselves or others'; 1.03(c)-(d); 1.07(c) minimum necessary; 1.07(d) notice before disclosure; 1.07(j) court orders: ask the court to withdraw or limit the order or keep records under seal; 1.14; 1.17(a)-(b)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on socialworkers.org (summarizing fetch with short quotes; the page shows the 2021 code). Amendments were to be voted 2026-11-18; recheck by 2026-12-15.

sources.cite: ASWB Examination Guidebook (August 2026), Clinical and Masters content outlines: I Values and Ethics (Clinical 36%, Masters 35%); II Assessment and Planning (32%, 33%); III Intervention and Practice (32% each); the 2026 blueprints in use from 2026-08-03
sources.note: Relayed from the REQ-288 sessions (read in full 2026-11-14 for REQ-286); not re-read for this case.

brief.situation: You are a licensed independent clinical social worker at a school-based health center in a Washington high school. Lily Tran, 15 (a fictional student), asks to talk during lunch. She says she has been having panic attacks before tests and wants counseling, but she does not want her parents to know. You have a 40-minute period.
